title: FormBuilder
wrapsNative: MonarchTabs for Build and Preview, Menu for the field palette, List with ForEach.onMove in edit mode and accessibilityActions Move up and Move down for the field list, sheet(item:) with NavigationStack, Form, Picker(.menu) and Toggle for field settings, and Form of MonarchFieldRenderer for the preview
summary: A recipe, not a component: a form builder on a phone, with Build and Preview tabs, an Add a field menu, a reorderable list of fields, a settings sheet per field and a live preview rendered by MonarchFieldRenderer.
whenToUse: When people design their own forms in an app (intake, surveys, request forms) and the questions are stored as MonarchFormFieldDefinition data.
whenNotToUse: To fill in a form, render it with MonarchSchemaDrivenForm or MonarchFieldRenderer alone. For a fixed form the app defines, use MonarchFormField and the form controls directly.
api: MonarchTabs("Form builder", selection: $tab, items: [MonarchTabsItem("Build", value: "build"), MonarchTabsItem("Preview", value: "preview")])
Menu { ForEach(palette, id: \.self) { type in Button(typeName(type)) { fields.append(MonarchFormFieldDefinition(…)) } } } label: { Label("Add a field", systemImage: "plus") }
List { ForEach(fields) { field in … }.onMove { fields.move(fromOffsets: $0, toOffset: $1) } }.environment(\.editMode, .constant(.active))
View.sheet(item: $editing) { NavigationStack { Form { MonarchTextField(…); Picker("Type", selection:) {…}.pickerStyle(.menu); Toggle("Required", isOn:) } } }

options.name: fields
options.description: The form, owned by the app in @State; the same data MonarchFieldRenderer and MonarchSchemaDrivenForm render and the app stores. Definitions are structs with var properties, so the settings sheet edits them through a Binding.

options.name: palette
options.description: The field types the builder offers, named by an app function; the Add a field menu and the Type picker use it.

options.name: settings
options.description: The settings sheet of one field: question, type, required, and any type-specific settings (options, limits) the app supports.

options.name: preview
options.description: MonarchFieldRenderer for every visible field, with answers kept in @State so conditions can be tried.

states.name: build
states.description: The Add a field menu, then the fields in a list in edit mode, each with its type, a required mark as text, a reorder control and an Edit button.

states.name: empty
states.description: MonarchEmptyState says there are no fields yet.

states.name: editing
states.description: A sheet with the question, the type, Required, Remove field and Done. A blank question shows an error.

states.name: preview
states.description: The form as people will fill it in, rendered by MonarchFieldRenderer in a Form.

appearance: MonarchTabs, the system menu, list, sheet and form around Monarch text, fields and buttons. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components and the system controls; the type line uses the muted text role.
platformNotes: The web FormBuilder is one component with three columns on wide screens (palette, field list, settings) and fewer on smaller ones; a phone has no room for side-by-side panes, so Build and Preview are tabs, the palette is a system Menu behind Add a field and each field's settings open in a sheet. Every part exists already (MonarchTabs, MonarchFieldRenderer, the system list reordering that reorderable-list documents), so iOS keeps it a recipe, as Android does. Android uses a DropdownMenu, a ModalBottomSheet, MonarchSelect and MonarchSwitchRow; iOS uses Menu, sheet with presentationDetents, Picker(.menu) and Toggle, which are what select and switch are on iOS. Android uses MonarchReorderableList; iOS uses ForEach.onMove in edit mode with the Move up and Move down accessibility actions from the reorderable-list recipe. MonarchFormFieldDefinition is a struct with var properties on iOS, so fields are edited in place through a Binding instead of rebuilt. The web's condition editor, duplicate, undo after remove, maximum field count and the full per-type settings (options, limits, accepted files) are not in the recipe: the app adds the settings it supports to the sheet, and MonarchConditionEditor for logic.
accessibility: Build and Preview are MonarchTabs, with the selected state.
Each field row is one element with its question and type; it has the accessibility actions Move up and Move down as the drag equivalent, and each move is announced with the new position.
Each Edit button is named Edit and the question, so the buttons can be told apart.
The type and required mark are text under the question, not colour.
Settings controls are labelled: the question is a MonarchTextField with an error for a blank question, the type a Picker and Required a Toggle.
The preview is the real form, with MonarchFieldRenderer's labels, required marks and errors.
edgeCases: The list is a scrolling List: make it the screen's list, or give it a bounded height inside a scrolling page.
Removing the field that is being edited closes the sheet; the settings binding reads the field by id, so a field removed elsewhere cannot crash the sheet.
Changing the type keeps the question; settings that belong to the old type are dropped by the app.
The list stays in edit mode so the reorder controls are always shown; an app that also deletes by swipe adds onDelete or switches edit mode with EditButton.
